name: Tutorial
description: Interactive guided tutorial overlay with step-based walkthrough. Each step has title, description, optional target element selector for highlighting, optional overflowHidden toggle, optional renderExtra callback for custom content, and onEnter/onLeave lifecycle hooks. Dark overlay with tooltip-style step cards positioned near highlighted targets. Steps can be navigated via Next/Previous buttons or skipped entirely. 'Show on launch' checkbox persisted to user prefs. Final step shows completion summary with option to re-run or close. Steps cover: welcome intro, canvas panning/zoom, menu bar, terminal tool, dev tool, markdown viewer, theme toggle, plugin cards, plugin list panel, arrange panel, keyboard shortcuts, stay connected (external links), thank you (completion). Tooltip positioning prefers below target → above → right → left → center fallback, clamped within viewport at max-width 360px.

interface.constructor: constructor() — Creates three div elements appended to document.body: .tutorial-overlay (fixed fullscreen dark transparent backdrop, display:none), .tutorial-tooltip (positioned step card, display:none), and .tutorial-ring (absolute border highlight for target elements, display:none). Registers document-level keydown listener (onKeydown) for Escape (close), ArrowRight/Enter (next step), ArrowLeft (previous step). Listener is a no-op when overlay is hidden.

methods.name: start
methods.description: Stores optional onClose callback, resets stepIdx to 0, sets overlay display:flex and tooltip visible, calls showStep() to render the first step (Welcome intro).

methods.name: getShowOnLaunch
methods.description: Returns the internal showOnLaunch flag. Updated on final step when 'Do not show this again' checkbox state is read before closing.

methods.name: destroy
methods.description: Removes the document keydown listener, then removes overlay, tooltip, and ring elements from DOM if they have a parent.

lifecycle.created_by: App constructor — instantiated once as Tutorial singleton
lifecycle.destroyed_by: Lives for the duration of the renderer process; DOM elements removed only on destroy() or window close
